result.title: PhysMamba: Selective State Space Models as Learned Articulated Body Simulators
result.comment: CVPR 2026 Workshop on Physically Grounded Human Perception and Modeling -- 1st PhysHuman
result.summary: We introduce the first learned articulated body simulator based on a selective state space model (SSM), called PhysMamba. PhysMamba predicts next-frame full-body state from position, rotation, and joint-action history, without velocity inputs. We compare four architectures under partial- and full-observation inputs and three training protocols. The from-scratch rollout training protocol gives Mamba2 strong short- and mid-horizon accuracy under partial observation (s10 = 43 mm, 2/50 diverged), while the two-stage teacher-based rollout protocol stabilizes GRU but fails for Mamba2. With CUDA graph compilation, Mamba2 reaches 0.107 ms per frame (9,334 FPS) on an H100 GPU, within 1.1$\times$ of GRU's un-compiled throughput, adding under 1% latency to a 30 Hz HMR pipeline and enabling integration as a differentiable physics module for video-based mesh recovery.

AI.brief_summary: PhysMamba 提出基于选择性状态空间模型（Mamba2）的可学习关节体模拟器，由位置、旋转与关节动作历史预测下一帧全身状态，无需速度输入，并在部分/全观测与不同训练协议下比较四种架构的精度与效率。
AI.relevance_reason: 面向多模态推理主线的联系较间接：其「Mamba 作为循环式 latent 状态更新器、逐步 rollout 预测下一状态」的结构或可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态生成、时序更新与部分观测下的信息保持问题，但论文本身不涉及 VLM 推理或视觉证据使用。
